# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-write / shadow-read capable) throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches by cohort; the legacy system remains fully operational as the system of record for unmigrated users until all cohorts are complete and validated.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — ~2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, tax calculation, payment method tokenization, and refund handling, with 100% parity on a 500-transaction synthetic test suite; rollback procedure has been tested and confirmed to restore a user to legacy billing in under 15 minutes.

**Cohort selection:** Internal employees and opted-in low-risk beta users (single currency, no active disputes, monthly plans only).

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum, including at least one full billing cycle.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Invoice accuracy ≥99.9%, no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents, support ticket volume for billing within 10% of baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (30% of users — ~12,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Eng, Finance, and Support leads; dual-write reconciliation job shows <0.05% discrepancy rate over the pilot's billing cycle.

**Cohort selection:** Broader mix including multiple currencies, annual plans, and users with saved payment methods — but excluding enterprise/contract customers and users with active billing disputes.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, staggered in weekly sub-batches of ~3,000–4,000 to limit blast radius.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Payment failure rate for migrated cohort within 0.5 percentage points of legacy baseline; reconciliation discrepancy rate <0.05% sustained across two consecutive billing cycles.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (50% of users — ~20,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; on-call and support teams trained and staffed for full-volume cutover; automated reconciliation and alerting dashboards live and validated against Phase 2 data.

**Cohort selection:** All remaining standard users, excluding the final reserved edge-case cohort (Phase 4).

**Duration:** 2–3 weeks in daily or twice-weekly sub-batches.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Sustained metrics within thresholds defined below for 10 consecutive days with no rollback events.

---

## Phase 4: Long Tail & Closure (remaining ~15% of users — ~6,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 exit criteria met; all known edge cases (enterprise contracts, disputed accounts, non-standard currencies, legacy grandfathered pricing) have documented migration procedures and Finance sign-off.

**Cohort selection:** Enterprise accounts, disputed/flagged accounts, and any manually-held-back edge cases.

**Duration:** 2–4 weeks; final batch migrated only after individual validation of each edge-case account.

**Note:** Decommissioning of the legacy billing system is explicitly **out of scope for this phase** and is not scheduled until a separate post-migration phase begins after a minimum 30-day parallel-run stabilization period following completion of Phase 4, during which the legacy system remains live as a fallback and audit reference.

---

## Halt Metric

If the **payment transaction failure rate for a migrated cohort exceeds 2% over any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout is automatically halted for new batches, and the current batch is evaluated for rollback.

Additional halt triggers:
- Invoice/reconciliation discrepancy rate exceeds **0.5%** for any batch.
- More than **3 Sev-1 incidents** attributable to the new billing system within a 7-day period.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double billing occurs during dual-write window due to race conditions between old and new systems | Implement idempotency keys and a reconciliation job that flags and auto-refunds duplicate charges within 1 hour | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate correctly, causing failed renewals for migrated users | Run a token-validation dry run against the payment processor sandbox before each batch and require 99.5% token migration success before batch starts | Payments Platform Team
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during peak migration batches | Stagger batch sizes, pre-train support staff per phase, and stand up a dedicated billing-migration support queue with escalation SLAs | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Regulatory or tax miscalculation in new system for specific jurisdictions | Run parallel tax calculation comparison (old vs new) for every invoice during Phases 1–3 and require Finance/Tax sign-off before expanding to new jurisdictions | Finance/Tax Compliance Lead
RISK: Rollback of a batch is delayed or fails, leaving users in an inconsistent billing state | Test rollback procedure before each phase and cap rollback execution time at 15 minutes per batch via automated runbook | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 4
